description: Hi! I'm Ritul, a high school junior and Robotics Club President with a Software Development certification and experience building multi-agent AI tools. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, I built AEGIS-MC—an autonomous edge-AI safety and triage system designed to protect astronauts during deep-space missions with zero cloud dependency.
summary: AEGIS Mission Control (AEGIS-MC) is an edge-AI space exploration safety and triage system designed to protect astronauts during high-risk extravehicular activities (EVAs) and deep-space missions. When communication delays with Earth make real-time ground support impossible, AEGIS runs entirely locally with zero cloud dependency to provide instant biometric monitoring, pre-EVA checklist verification, real-time telemetry analysis, and peer-to-peer crew mesh safety. By combining local heuristic triage with an intuitive interface, AEGIS ensures crews stay protected, autonomous, and connected when every second counts.
details:
• What it does & How it works: AEGIS-MC acts as an autonomous local edge-AI safety supervisor. Before any spacewalk, astronauts use the app's local interface to complete mandatory pre-EVA health and suit checks. While outside, it continuously monitors telemetry and local sensor data offline, instantly flagging anomalies without needing a connection to Earth.
  • Intended Impact: Drastically reduces mission risk, eliminates communication-delay bottlenecks, and provides immediate life-support triage for crew members in deep space or on lunar/Martian surfaces.
  • Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used: Developed using modern web/software development tools, local edge-AI frameworks, and responsive UI components designed for seamless tablet and mobile use in astronaut gear.
  • Creativity & Considerations: Built with zero cloud-dependency to solve the extreme latency challenges of deep-space exploration, prioritizing cost-efficiency, rapid offline execution, and high-contrast accessibility for crew environments.
